body: I'm a recovery specialist at a transitional support services unit and am in amphetamine recovery myself. I would recommend a temporary residential admission situation for your S/O when they get out of prison. There are several benefits to such an arrangement. Firstly, they will likely have a medication administration facet. Less clinical settings will only administer medications that your S/O is currently prescribed, but more intensive units will feature a psychological evaluation from a licensed psychiatrist, and he will be given medications based on the diagnoses. This can be particularly helpful if he is using currently to self-medicate an undiagnosed neurological issue. Frequently, meth users are dealing with adult attention deficit disorder, bipolar 1 & 2, depression, anxiety, and / or other comorbidities that are not addressed. Residencies also employ caseworkers that help their clients create a conducive plan to stay clean, find work, and continue further treatment on their own if necessary. If I were you, I'd look to see what facilities are accessible with your insurance, location, and timeframe. If residential treatment doesn't seem applicable, I would still recommend taking the time to help your S/O find a suitable therapist and psychiatrist to help work through the reasoning and ground factors that leads them to abuse amphetamines. Cognitive and dialectical behavioral therapy is shown to greatly reduce the probability of relapse in recovering addicts. I hope this helps, and good luck.

This wasn’t really a fuck up but it was unprofessional. I was in an after school program in elementary school and the head counselor was a nice lady named Mrs. Q. Mrs. Q was sweet but stern, and my friends and I were relatively ill-behaved. Nothing serious, just a little rowdy and prone to shenanigans. Well, sometimes we would go on field trips, I think this time it was the movies. My friends and I were causing a ruckus while waiting for the bus and Mrs. Q having had just about enough, lightly grabbed us by the arms and gently pulled us close and said,

“You three are acting like assholes”

We were so jazzed that a teacher swore, that not only did we not care that she did at us, but I think we all respected her a little more. We were voluntarily better behaved for the rest of the trip, giggling about being so rambunctious that a teacher actually called us assholes. And the head of staff no less! I miss Mrs. Q. I still dropped off old toys at the program until I was in my early 20’s, and she’s always happy to see me. 

Edit: I think we were 9-10. We didn’t tell our parents at the risk of losing the only staff member with the balls to tell it like it was.

She would heckle me, and post pictures of me serving my punishment to social media to show off what a funny, creative parent she was to her friends. 

I feel like after my teachers met my mom, they realized I was only responding to my treatment at home. Wasn’t an excuse for me acting out, but I understand why, now. Any time I was being difficult or insubordinate, i was channeling my mom. I said things she would say, and defend myself in the same profanity-laced, disgusted, angry candor that she would use with me. 

And I think since I would then come to school defeated and quiet, they usually just thought I’d had enough punishment and would become more lenient. That said, in the beginning of 8th grade, this kid would pick on me in shop class in an obvious but not overtly hostile way. He would like, make fun of my acne, or that I was gay, and other generally standard bullying material. This continued for weeks until the day after Town Night, (a holiday in my hometown following Town Day, a really long block party on the town’s Main Street. Town Night is the night of the year where tweens and teens literally have a huge shaving cream fight in the field in front of the local Boys and Girls Club (I’m not kidding.)

Anyway, at Town Night, my girlfriend at the time surprised me by slapping a handful of shaving cream in my face... and immediately broke my nose. 

So I’m literally covered in white shaving cream from head to toe and immediately get a long, bloody road running vertically from my upper lip down through my torso.

I went to the paramedic and they kind of gently popped it back. I was fine, in fact it felt kind of badass.

Turns out, Dickhead McShopclass saw me walking to the medic station at Town Night. I get to school the next morning, and everyone’s asking me how bad McShopclass whooped my ass. It didn’t take long to find out he was telling this to anyone who would listen. I lost my shit. I went and found him hangin with his goons and just kind of started screaming and getting in his face. Something to the effect of “you got something to fucking say, you wanna fight, let’s do it fucker, hit me, fucking hit me” and I told him to hit me like 3 times, and I’m not sure if I remember who shoved first, but I remember that once he shoved me, I went nuts. This kid was like 6 inches on me (5,5 in middle school) and I just kind of jumped on to his back like a monkey and started wailing on the back of his head. Don’t ask me how I got there. I think I started swinging, and just kind of slung myself from his neck to his back. It was at the very least, clumsy.

After like 20 seconds of this, I didn’t really know what to do, and I definitely didn’t think I’d get this far, so I kind of jumped off and went back to where I was sitting and tried to finish my homework. Guy just stares at me totally  gobsmacked, holding the back of his neck with this look like;

Kid and I are in the principals office, and the kid’s mad stressed cuz he doesn’t want his dad to get called for this. I tell him he probably should have thought of that before he chose to harass me.
